title: Design-unbiased statistical learning in survey sampling
what_it_holds: Subsampling Rao-Blackwell (SRB). Sample s is split into a training subsample s1 and test subsample s2 (known subsampling design q, main case SRS); a linear or ML model is fitted on s1 and test errors are projected to the population; the estimator is averaged over subsamples and is exactly design-unbiased for any model. Variance given as V = E1[V2(Yhat_1M | s1)] minus E_p[V_q(Yhat_1M | s)], with a jackknife variance for the delete-one case. Under SRS the delete-one theorem gives variance (1 - n/N)(1/n)E(tau) + o(1), so the leading term carries the fpc; the general formulas show no explicit (1 - n/N) factor. Cluster sampling is not covered. [abstract read; variance details are from a fetch-tool summary of the full text, not read by me directly]
